app.title: AudioLibro Libre
app.tagline: Turn a book into an audiobook. Free, on your own computer, nothing sent to the internet.
steps.label: Wizard steps
legal.title: Important legal notice
legal.text: You must have the rights to the book you convert (it is yours, it is in the public domain, or you have its owner's permission). This tool does not include or distribute copyrighted books.
legal.accept: I confirm I have the right to convert the books I will use.
legal.footer: Remember: only use books you have rights to. AudioLibro Libre does not include or distribute copyrighted books. Everything is processed on your computer.
sys.title: Something is missing on your computer
sys.ffmpeg_missing: ffmpeg was not found (needed to create the MP3 files).
sys.espeak_missing: espeak-ng was not found (needed to pronounce the text correctly).
sys.how: How to install it: with Docker it is already included. On Windows, run install.bat again. On Mac: brew install ffmpeg espeak-ng. On Linux: sudo apt install ffmpeg espeak-ng. Then reload this page.
s1.title: 1. Upload your book
s1.explain: Choose the book file (EPUB, PDF, Word, TXT or Markdown). The app opens it on your computer, extracts the text, removes page numbers, headers and footnotes, and detects the chapters. Nothing leaves your machine. If the PDF is scanned (page photos) its text is recognised with OCR, which takes longer.
s1.language_help: Used to suggest voices. You can change it in step 3.
s1.reading: Reading the book… (long books can take a few seconds)
s1.demo_title: First time? Try a sample book
s1.demo_text: It uses a public-domain excerpt of Don Quixote (or Pride and Prejudice in English). In about 2 minutes you will have your first audiobook.
s1.projects_empty: No projects yet. When you upload a book it will appear here so you can pick it up any time.
s1.delete_confirm: Delete “{title}” and all its audio? This cannot be undone.
s2.title: 2. Review the text
s2.explain: This is what will be read aloud. Page numbers, footnotes and end-of-line hyphens have already been removed and chapters detected. Check the titles, fix the text if needed and untick anything you do not want to hear (index, acknowledgements…).
s2.author: Author
s2.skip_hint: Parts people usually do not want to hear (index, credits, acknowledgements…) were unticked automatically. Tick them again if you want them.
s2.none_selected: Tick at least one chapter to continue.
s2.select_one: Pick a chapter from the list to see and edit its text.
s3.title: 3. Choose the voice and settings
s3.explain: Here you decide how the book will sound. Voices are downloaded once (about 60 MB for Piper; Kokoro downloads a 330 MB model) and then work offline. Press “Listen to sample” to hear 10 seconds before processing the whole book.
s3.voice_help: Each voice has its own license. All the ones shown allow commercial use.
s3.attribution: Requires attribution (added automatically to the credits)
s3.speaker: Speaker
s3.pause_c: Pause at the end of each chapter (seconds)
help.speed: 1.0 is normal speed. Lower is slower; higher is faster. For audiobooks 0.9 to 1.1 usually works well.
help.pause_p: Silence left between one paragraph and the next. More pause = calmer reading.
help.pause_c: Silence at the end of a chapter, before the next one starts.
help.read_titles: If enabled, each chapter starts by saying its title (for example “Chapter one”).
help.pron: If the voice mispronounces a name, acronym or foreign word, write how it should sound. For example: “NASA” → “nasa”, “Hermione” → “her my oh nee”.
s3.pron_explain: Optional. Write the word as it appears in the book and, next to it, how you want it to sound (spelled as it is read aloud).
s3.est_title: Before you start: what you will need
s3.est_time_unmeasured: (initial estimate: it will be refined with your computer once you start)
s3.disk_warn: There may not be enough disk space. Free some space before starting.
s3.ram_warn: Your computer has little memory. Close other programs before starting.
s4.title: 4. Generate the audio
s4.explain: The text is split into small pieces and turned into speech one by one. Each piece is saved to disk as soon as it is done: if you pause, cancel or the computer shuts down you lose nothing and can continue where you left off.
s4.state.cancelled: Stopped. Your progress is saved and you can resume.
s4.listen_none: No audio in this chapter yet.
s4.safe: You can close this tab: generation keeps going while the app is open. If you close the app, press “Resume” when you come back.
s5.title: 5. Export your audiobook
s5.explain: The audiobook is created with title, author and cover, and with levelled volume. You can pick a single M4B file (with chapter markers, ideal for phones) and/or one MP3 per chapter. Everything is bundled in a ZIP to download.
s5.cover_help: JPG or PNG image. If the book came with a cover, it appears here.
s5.meta: It will be saved with this data: “{title}” by {author}.
s5.credits: The ZIP includes CREDITOS.txt with the voice license. If the voice requires attribution, keep that file when sharing the audio.
s5.incomplete: Some audio is still missing. Go back to step 4 and finish generating.
tutorial.title: 2-minute tutorial
tutorial.intro: We will turn an excerpt of Don Quixote (public domain) into an audiobook. Just follow these steps:
tutorial.s1: The sample book loads and its chapters are detected.
tutorial.s2: You review the text (it is already clean; you can leave it as is).
tutorial.s3: You pick the recommended voice, download the model (about 60 MB, first time only) and listen to the sample.
tutorial.s4: You press “Start generating” and wait a couple of minutes.
tutorial.s5: You export and download the ZIP with the MP3 files.

errors.empty_book.msg: No text was found in the book.
errors.empty_book.hint: Check that the file is not empty. If it is a scanned PDF and it fails, check that Tesseract (OCR) is installed.
errors.epub_invalid.msg: This EPUB is damaged or is not a valid EPUB.
errors.epub_invalid.hint: Try downloading it again, or convert it to TXT with a program such as Calibre.
errors.epub_drm.msg: This EPUB is DRM-protected and cannot be read.
errors.epub_drm.hint: Use an unprotected copy of a book you have rights to.
errors.file_too_big.msg: The file is too big (maximum {max_mb} MB).
errors.file_too_big.hint: Check that you chose the right file.
errors.unreadable_text.msg: The text of the file could not be read.
errors.unreadable_text.hint: Save it as TXT with UTF-8 encoding and try again.
errors.voice_unknown.hint: Pick another one from the list in step 3.
errors.voice_not_selected.msg: You have not chosen a voice yet.
errors.voice_not_selected.hint: Go back to step 3, choose a voice and download it.
errors.voice_not_installed.msg: The chosen voice is not downloaded yet.
errors.voice_not_installed.hint: In step 3 press “Download voice” (internet is only needed for this).
errors.voice_unsupported.msg: This voice uses a format the app does not support.
errors.no_chapters_selected.msg: No chapter is ticked for conversion.
errors.no_chapters_selected.hint: In step 2 tick at least one chapter.
errors.no_chapters.hint: Add at least one chapter with text.
errors.espeak_missing.msg: espeak-ng is missing on your computer.
errors.espeak_missing.hint: With Docker it is already included. On Windows run install.bat again; on Mac: brew install espeak-ng; on Linux: sudo apt install espeak-ng. Then restart the app.
errors.espeak_failed.hint: Restart the app. If it keeps happening, see docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md.
errors.ffmpeg_missing.msg: ffmpeg is missing on your computer.
errors.ffmpeg_missing.hint: With Docker it is already included. On Windows run install.bat again; on Mac: brew install ffmpeg; on Linux: sudo apt install ffmpeg. Then restart the app.
errors.ffmpeg_failed.msg: The audio file could not be created.
errors.ffmpeg_failed.hint: Check that you have free disk space and try again.
errors.no_internet.msg: Could not connect to download the voice.
errors.no_internet.hint: Check your internet connection. It is only needed to download the voice the first time.
errors.download_failed.hint: Try again in a few minutes.
errors.download_corrupt.msg: The voice file downloaded incomplete or damaged.
errors.download_cancelled.hint: You can try again whenever you like.
errors.export_incomplete.hint: Go back to step 4 and let generation finish.
errors.export_already_running.msg: An export is already in progress.
errors.job_not_found.hint: Go back to step 1 and open it from “My projects”.
errors.job_running.msg: It cannot be changed while generating.
errors.job_already_running.msg: This project is already being generated.
errors.job_not_running.msg: This project is not being generated right now.
errors.job_not_running.hint: Reload the page to see its state.
errors.cover_invalid.msg: The cover must be a JPG or PNG image.
errors.cover_missing.hint: You can upload one in step 5.
errors.preview_empty.msg: No audio has been generated for that chapter yet.
errors.preview_empty.hint: Wait a few seconds for the first piece to be generated.
errors.unexpected.hint: Press “Resume” to continue without losing what is done. If it repeats, see docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md. Technical detail: {detail}
errors.network.hint: Check that the AudioLibro Libre window (or Docker) is still open and reload the page.
errors.pdf_encrypted.hint: Remove the password with your PDF reader (print to an unprotected PDF) and upload it again. Only use books you have rights to.
errors.pdf_invalid.msg: This PDF cannot be read: it is damaged or not a valid PDF.
errors.pdf_invalid.hint: Try downloading it again or saving it as PDF once more from your reader.
errors.docx_invalid.msg: This Word document cannot be read.
errors.docx_invalid.hint: Open it in Word or LibreOffice and save it again as .docx (not .doc).
errors.ocr_missing.msg: This PDF looks scanned (page photos) and Tesseract, the program that recognises text, is missing.
errors.ocr_missing.hint: With Docker it is already included. On Windows: install Tesseract from https://github.com/UB-Mannheim/tesseract/wiki ticking the language you need, then restart the app. On Mac: brew install tesseract tesseract-lang. On Linux: sudo apt install tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng. Then upload the PDF again.
errors.ocr_lang_missing.msg: Tesseract is installed but the language “{lang}” is missing.
errors.ocr_lang_missing.hint: Install the language pack: on Linux sudo apt install tesseract-ocr-eng (or tesseract-ocr-spa); on Mac brew install tesseract-lang; on Windows run the Tesseract installer again and tick the language.
errors.ocr_failed.hint: Try a better-quality PDF or convert it to text with another program. Technical detail: {detail}
s1.ocr_progress: Recognising text (OCR): page {done} of {total}. A scanned book can take several minutes; do not close this tab.
s1.ocr_note: Scanned PDF: recognising its text needs Tesseract, which is not installed. You only need it for PDFs that are page photos; everything else works.
s1.ocr_how: How to install it: with Docker it is already included. Windows: install Tesseract (UB-Mannheim) with the language you need. Mac: brew install tesseract tesseract-lang. Linux: sudo apt install tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng.
s5.formats: What do you want to create?
s5.fmt_m4b: A single M4B file with chapter markers (recommended)
s5.m4b_hint: Works in Apple Books, VLC, Audiobookshelf, Smart Audiobook Player and most audiobook apps.
errors.export_format_none.msg: You have not chosen any format.
errors.export_format_none.hint: Tick M4B, MP3 or both and press “Create” again.
s3.engine_kokoro: Kokoro — more natural, but much slower (330 MB download)
help.engine: Piper turns a whole book into audio in minutes or a few hours, even on a modest computer. Kokoro sounds more natural but takes several times longer (a 300-page book can take about 3 hours on a 4-core laptop) and uses more memory (≈1 GB). Listen to the 10-second sample with each before deciding.
